meta.dataset: Punctual Pros advertising program - cheap CTV, LSA, new-mover mail and weather-triggered creative (with Fair Harbor DTC appendix)
meta.portfolio_company: Punctual Pros (Broad Sky Partners) incl. Horvath Home Services (Ocean/Monmouth NJ); appendix: Fair Harbor
meta.method: CTV platform terms, benchmarks and franchisor brand promises were fetched from the cited pages on 2026-10-06 (WebFetch/curl); where a page returned 403 or was gated, the figure comes from the search-engine result for that URL and the item is marked retrieval status='search snippet'. Territory facts were computed from repo data: Punctual Pros ZIP coverage (248 flagged zips, 1,001,408 housing units, 61 Tier-I zips with 336,002 units), data/sales deed feeds (trailing-12-month arm's-length residential sales by county; 33% of Lancaster/York/Cumberland/Dauphin residential sales are pre-1980 homes), Punctual Pros storm-event history (NOAA monthly event counts) and the Punctual Pros demand model (NWS weather-response plans). Media plans are computed in code from the benchmark items with explicit formulas in each plan's 'model' field; every output is an estimate. Creative is original sample copy written to each brand's published guarantee language.

territory_facts.notes: Dauphin (85 sales) and Franklin (0 in trailing 12 months) are under-counted in the deed feed, so 2,300/month is a floor-adjusted estimate (~24.9k counted + ~3k gap)/12.

caveats: No public home-services CTV cost-per-site-visit or CPL benchmark was found; the $12 cost per visit is an assumption anchored on DTC case studies and must be replaced by the week-8 read.
Mail lead rate (1.0% per piece) is deliberately below ANA prospect response (4-5%) and vendor new-mover claims (4.9%); treat both as upper bounds.

SearchLight and LocaliQ disagree on search CPL ($104 blended Jan 2026 vs $128 HVAC Apr 2024-Mar 2025) because of different samples and lead definitions; plans use SearchLight because it also reports book rates and closed revenue.
Mister Sparky's national guarantee ('the repair is free') differs from the Lancaster location page ('we'll pay you back'); creative uses the safe line until PP confirms.

All offers are illustrative; prices, discounts and membership terms must come from PP's price book and Authority Brands' marketing standards. Multi-brand ads need franchisor approval (assumption about franchise agreement terms).

Amazon Sponsored TV self-serve is limited to Amazon Brand Registry sellers; Spectrum Reach's footprint likely excludes PP territories (Comcast and Altice/Optimum are the incumbents) - both kept for completeness, flagged low fit.
CPM ranges for Disney, Roku, Samsung, Tubi and Paramount come from third-party guides, not the platforms; zip targeting on Roku self-serve and MNTN was not confirmed on the pages read.
Trade mix (50/35/15) and 40% gross margin are planning assumptions; replace with ServiceTitan actuals.
meta.strategy_summary: Punctual Pros sells three franchise brands whose core promise is punctuality, so the advertising program should sell the promise (One Hour's 'Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!', Ben Franklin's $5-a-minute guarantee, Mister Sparky's 'America's On-Time Electrician') rather than invent new claims. Google Local Services Ads are the cheapest high-intent leads in the category ($39-57 per lead at a ~44% book rate, SearchLight Feb 2026), so LSA is the always-on base and is managed through reviews and fast answer rates rather than bids. Self-serve CTV has dropped to $50-$500 minimums and roughly $15-40 CPMs with zip targeting (Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads, YouTube on TV screens), which lets a ~$22M franchisee buy TV in its ~240 zips without paying for the whole Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA. CTV's job is to make the brand familiar before the furnace fails and to lift branded search and LSA conversion, so it is judged on cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift, not completion rate (which is ~94-99% by construction). New-mover direct mail is the highest-intent prospect list a home-services company can get: county deed records show ~2,300 arm's-length residential sales a month in the PA core and ~1,150 on the Jersey Shore, each a household that must pick an HVAC, plumbing and electrical provider within months. One in three of those PA buyers bought a pre-1980 home, which drives the Ben Franklin and Mister Sparky older-home inspection offers and the CTV zip weighting toward older housing stock (Punctual Pros ZIP coverage older-housing share). The weather index ties it together: NWS alerts for PP's zones (the demand model's weather-response plans) trigger budget multipliers and creative swaps 12-36 hours before demand spikes, so spend lands when calls are about to rise rather than after phones are already full. The same deed feed becomes the CTV and Meta audience (address-matched households) and the mail list, so one new mover sees a coordinated welcome across mailbox, TV and phone, measured against a random holdout. Test first with an 8-week, $50k/month Central PA pilot: LSA profile and review clean-up, a zip-level CTV geo holdout in the 61 Tier-I zips, and a mail-versus-holdout new-mover drip, all on unique call-tracking numbers in ServiceTitan. If measured cost per booked job beats the modelled ~$185-200 blended, scale to the Jersey Shore (zip-only CTV) and then a regional Mid-Atlantic program, which also leaves a documented, attributed customer-acquisition engine for the exit data room.
